name: SAP NG WU
description: Sap Ng Wu (十五湖) is a climbing game for three or four players using an 84-card Chinese domino pack. Players in turn beat the previous play with a higher card or combination or pass; the player who played the highest takes the cards as wu (winning cards). The first to collect 15 or more wu declares a win (sik wu) and receives chip payments from the others.

Players in turn beat the previous play with a higher card or combination or pass; the player who played the highest takes the cards as wu (winning cards). The first to collect 15 or more wu declares a win (sik wu) and receives chip payments from the others.

Country/Region of Origin: China
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game

Minimum Players: 3
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 3
Partnerships: None

Type: 84-card Chinese domino pack (十五湖紙牌); 21 tile types with four copies of each
Jokers: Not included

84-card Chinese domino pack (15 lakes playing-cards)
Chips for payment (optional)
Table space
Pack shuffled and spread face down; players take one card at a time anticlockwise from dealer until all taken. Three players: 28 cards each; four players: 21 each.

items.text: Wu Han games: Related climbing games from Hubei (Wu Han): military divided by red/black spots; player obliged to beat if able; bonus scores for particular cards among winning cards.

Si Chuan Luan Chuo (乱戳): Played in Si Chuan with 川牌; different ranking (e.g. middle three equal, lower four equal); 16+ wu to win; points and multipliers (番). Sometimes four players with one sitting out; talon of 3 cards.

Mā Huā Huā (抹花花): Northwest China (Shaanxi, Ningxia, Gansu); 48-card pack; three or four players (one sits out); special groups (happy cards, bull cards, pendulum, fish); 6+ pillars for one family, 11+ for two families.
